# Set-ZbxHousekeeping

## SYNOPSIS

Changes how long the server keeps history, trends, events and records.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxHousekeeping [-HousekeepingEventsMode <bool>] [-HousekeepingEventsTrigger <string>] [-HousekeepingEventsService <string>] [-HousekeepingEventsInternal <string>] [-HousekeepingEventsDiscovery <string>] [-HousekeepingEventsAutoregistration <string>] [-HousekeepingServicesMode <bool>] [-HousekeepingServices <string>] [-HousekeepingAuditMode <bool>] [-HousekeepingAudit <string>] [-HousekeepingSessionsMode <bool>] [-HousekeepingSessions <string>] [-HousekeepingHistoryMode <bool>] [-HousekeepingHistoryGlobal <bool>] [-HousekeepingHistory <string>] [-HousekeepingTrendsMode <bool>] [-HousekeepingTrendsGlobal <bool>] [-HousekeepingTrends <string>] [-CompressionStatus <bool>] [-CompressOlder <string>] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Set-ZbxHousekeeping cmdlet changes the housekeeping settings with housekeeping.update: each parameter given sets one setting, and every setting not given keeps its value. The housekeeper applies the new periods on its next run and deletes what is older. The command writes the settings only with -PassThru, -WhatIf shows what would change, and it needs a Super admin's connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Keep audit records for a year

```powershell
Set-ZbxHousekeeping -HousekeepingAuditMode $true -HousekeepingAudit '365d' -PassThru | Select-Object HousekeepingAuditMode, HousekeepingAudit
```

A period is a time with a unit; the housekeeper deletes older records on its next run.

### Example 2: Preview overriding every item's history period

```powershell
Set-ZbxHousekeeping -HousekeepingHistoryGlobal $true -HousekeepingHistory '90d' -WhatIf
```

With HousekeepingHistoryGlobal, the one period applies to every item; -WhatIf makes no change.
